medium_value.description: Add an explicit dependency and readiness matrix for model catalog entries, generated maps, Bridgebuilder registry generation, and Flatline model resolution, including the exact source of truth for each derived value and the command that validates freshness.
Add a release validation checklist that maps each KPI to one command, fixture, or artifact path, and states which checks are blocking before draft PR creation.

Clarify the no-publication constraint by defining whether creating a draft PR, pushing `feature/cycle-126-full-size`, generating an rc changelog entry, or preparing version metadata are allowed actions.

Define security review requirements for the new `params.beta_headers` catalog field, including allowed header names, validation of header values, and whether arbitrary catalog entries may inject transport headers.

Specify exact grep or semantic-search criteria for 'no 4.x id used as a default or current' and list allowed historical references that should not fail the check, such as changelog history, migration docs, or audit evidence.

Add explicit owner and evidence requirements for the deferred live ceiling probe, including when it must be run, where calibrated results are recorded, and what happens if the probe contradicts the catalog-derived ceiling.

Define the exact behavior when a catalog-derived 1M request proceeds but the provider rejects it at runtime, including envelope fields, exit code, retry behavior, and whether downstream `/ride`, review, and trajectory records mark the run as failed, degraded, or operator-actionable.

Specify how `claude-headless` is invoked, authenticated, timed out, retried, and isolated as a first-class dissent voice, including the exact detection rule for no Anthropic credential and what happens if headless is unavailable.

Add backwards-compatibility requirements for consumers of dissent envelopes and feedback files, including schema versioning for `input_ceiling`, `rejected_summary`, `failure_mode_derived`, and any new `voices_*` fields.

Define measurable A/B acceptance thresholds for the review and audit gold sets, including which metrics count as recall regression, allowable variance, fixture count, and the required artifact path for the report.

Clarify the `long` context-class detection algorithm by naming the session-model signal source, precedence order among session model, catalog, and `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS`, and behavior when the model is unknown or mixed across hops.

Add explicit tests for the kill switches preserving legacy behavior across all affected components, not only cheval: Bridgebuilder output defaults, temperature default, Flatline caps, and any routing aliases that remain intentionally unchanged under legacy mode.
Define a migration compatibility policy for changing the `cheap` alias to Sonnet 5, including affected roles, expected cost/latency impact, and which roles should explicitly move to `tiny` instead.

Add an explicit fixture inventory for the three real rejected dissent payloads and KF-004, including their file paths, expected derived fields, expected final findings, and expected sidecar or feedback output.

Specify how budget headroom is calculated for `CLAUDE.loa.md` and protocols, including whether byte, token, or character counts are authoritative and which files count toward the 20 percent protocol headroom target.

FR-3.1 must specify the mechanism by which a static skill include expresses a per-session context class. Options: (a) the include carries both class tables plus a one-line selection rule, or (b) a SessionStart hook writes the resolved class to `.run/` and the include references it. Also state the safe behaviour when the session model cannot be determined (agent-team teammates on Haiku 4.5, Claude Code plans without the 1M window, downstream mounts on 200K models) — `long` as an unconditional default sends a 200K session toward a 150K STOP threshold and context overflow.

Add kill switches for FR-2.1 (disable planning `claude-headless` as a voice, e.g. `adversarial_review.headless_as_voice: false`) and FR-2.2 (strict schema mode), and list them in the Security NFR alongside the two cheval switches.

FR-1.6 should state whether the per-voice cap covers output only or output plus thinking, and how it interacts with adaptive thinking (no explicit budget) versus a fixed `budget_tokens`; include a test for each mode.

Resolve the FR-1.4 wording: define the fallback when the count endpoint times out or errors (proceed with the byte bound? warn?), and reconcile 'conservative for the gate' with 'never the sole reason to preempt an unprobed entry' by stating the exact decision table (probed × estimator source × action).

Add a risk row for subscription usage caps: two headless-backed voices per review and audit across four sprints plus repair-loop calls draw on the Claude Code session budget; mitigate with the existing session-limit capture (`session-limit-capture.sh`) and a rule to degrade to one voice when the cap signal appears.
Give FR-3.3 a numeric pass criterion: gold-set sizes, the recall metric per set, the tolerance (e.g. no item lost; or ≥ baseline within N items), and how many runs per arm given model nondeterminism.
Express the FR-3.1 thresholds as a formula of the context window (e.g. per-read 2 %, per-file 5 %, session STOP 15 %) with the two classes as worked examples, rather than a second literal table.

Turn the appendix assumption '1M context is available without a beta header' into an explicit operator evidence step tied to G-1 (run `ceiling-probe-live.py` post-merge, record the result in the catalog `beta_headers`/`calibrated_at`), and pre-fill `beta_headers` for the 5-family entries from the provider documentation rather than leaving it empty by default.

FR-4.4 should specify that the `active_skill` recorder is write-once (short-circuit when the marker exists), where the marker lives (`.run/`), and the rollback rule when a later harness stops sending `active_skill` (implement-gate reverts to heuristic mode after N payloads without the field, rather than failing closed or open indefinitely).
Add a `.loa.config.yaml` key for the context class (with `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS` as an env override) so fleet operators can pin `standard` per mount, and list it in the migration addendum.

Re-slice the sprints so MVP items land first and FR-1 is not a single sprint: e.g. Sprint 1 = FR-1.1/1.3/1.4 (cheval, Python), Sprint 2 = FR-1.5/1.6/1.7 (BB TypeScript + dist, Flatline bash) with FR-2.1/2.2, and pull FR-3.1 forward; or state why one sprint can carry seven sub-items across three languages with test-first discipline.

Add a requirement to FR-4.2 that determines whether `model-permissions.yaml` (and any trust-store it feeds) is signature-verified, and if so, plan the operator re-signing step explicitly (operator-delegation pattern: agent stages entries, operator signs with the offline root key) with an acceptance test that the unsigned staged file fails closed rather than silently loading.

Justify or catalog-ize the 64K streaming / 16K non-streaming transport caps in FR-1.3 (e.g. a `transport.max_output_streaming` config with the rationale for each bound), since the models declare 128K output.
Add a traceability table mapping audit findings C1–C9 to FR-1.1–FR-1.7 and fix the executive summary, which says 'nine direct caps' but enumerates seven.
State the cost impact of remapping `cheap` from Sonnet 4.6 to Sonnet 5 for the three roles that consume it, and decide in the PRD (not the SDD) which of those roles move to `tiny`.

Mark UC-1 (a real 400K-token `/ride`) and the live ceiling behaviour as operator-validated post-merge, and define what the Sprint 4 'end-to-end goal validation' can actually exercise on a keyless host (pre-flight fixtures, two-voice dissent, budget gate).
Document the exit-code change in FR-1.1 (unprobed entries no longer exit 7 above 180K) in the migration addendum and audit existing tests and callers that assert exit 7.

Replace the KPI 'Real findings lost to schema rejection (this week's three fixtures)' with a durable metric such as rejected-payload rate over the full KF-004 fixture corpus and the `rejected_summary` count per envelope over the cycle.

Scope the FR-1.3 default `max_tokens` raise: specify whether the catalog-derived default (up to 64K) applies to every call or only to roles/callers that opt in, and add a risk row for provider output-rate-limit reservation (Anthropic estimates OTPM from `max_tokens` at request start), with a mitigation such as a per-role cap in the catalog or a `LOA_CHEVAL_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS` bound.

Add a requirement that the cost ledger, pricing ladder and budget breaker (cycle-125) handle the long-context premium tier: Anthropic prices input above 200K tokens at a higher rate. Specify the pricing-table field, the cost-report change, and a test that a 600K-token receipt is priced at the premium tier and evaluated by the breaker.

FR-2.1 should specify how the `claude-headless` voice selects its model (explicit `--model` from the configured primary voice or alias) and require the envelope to record the model id the hop actually reported, not the one requested, with a test that a mismatch is surfaced as `voice_model_attribution: mismatch`.

Replace the FR-4 acceptance 'grep for a 4.x id used as a default or current in live scripts returns nothing' with a checked-in lint (e.g. `tools/check-model-era.sh`) wired into CI, with defined semantics: which paths are 'live', which contexts count as 'default/current' (fallback maps, `--help`, default variables, comments saying current) versus legitimately retained catalog entries and migration docs.

Clarify in FR-1.1 whether the `warn` action fires for every request to an uncalibrated high-ceiling entry or only for requests above the last-probed value, and move the '180,000 last probed' constant into the catalog (per entry or per provider, e.g. `ceiling_calibration.last_probed`) rather than a code literal, so a probe result or a new provider needs a catalog edit only.

Specify Bridgebuilder behaviour when the default `opus` alias resolves to an HTTP Anthropic entry on a host without an Anthropic API key: fall back to the headless hop (mirroring FR-2.1) or fail with a named preflight error, and add it to the acceptance tests.

FR-2.2 should enumerate the rejection reasons recorded across the 31 KF-004 recurrences (not only missing `failure_mode`) and decide per reason: tolerate-and-derive, tolerate-and-mark, or sidecar+summary. Add a `rejected_reason_histogram` to the envelope metadata so the KF-004 closing evidence is measurable.

FR-2.3 must define how `verdict-derive.sh` locates the dissent envelope for a given feedback file (path convention per sprint and per `/bug` sprint), skip the check when no dissent ran, and state whether an 'accepted' rejected payload of HIGH/CRITICAL severity enters the critical+high count that drives the one-way CHANGES_REQUIRED rule.

blockers.concern: FR-4.4 adds a hook-chain recorder that flips active_skill_available to true on the first real payload, which switches implement-gate.sh into an authoritative branch the audit itself calls dead code. A never-exercised fence mode is activated at runtime by a side effect, potentially mid-cycle during this very run. The recorder also writes state from PreToolUse — in agent-teams mode from every teammate — contradicting the 'only the team lead writes .run/' rule and the 'no new per-call hook latency' NFR.
blockers.why_matters: The unattended run could block or start asking on its own writes partway through Sprint 4 with no operator present. G-5 says 'every fence that exists today still fires' but is silent about a new fence mode becoming live; the fence corpus has no cases for it.
blockers.location: FR-4.4, Non-Functional Requirements (Performance), Agent Teams rules, Success Criteria G-5
blockers.recommendation: Gate authoritative mode behind an explicit opt-in in .loa.config.yaml rather than a probe flip; ship a fixture corpus of real PreToolUse payloads (with and without active_skill, nested /run dispatch) and fence-corpus cases for the authoritative branch; make the recorder a one-shot write by the lead only, or record to the trajectory instead of .run.

blockers.concern: The PRD assumes 1M-context and 128K-output model capabilities are available on the target account and transport without requiring live verification before changing default gates.
blockers.why_matters: If the provider, account tier, transport, or required beta headers do not actually support these limits, the framework will move failures from deterministic pre-flight rejection to expensive late runtime failures across large unattended runs.
blockers.location: FR-1.1 Ceiling policy; Appendix assumptions; Technical Considerations
blockers.recommendation: Make capability verification a release-blocking prerequisite for enabling catalog-derived warn-and-proceed by default, or gate the new behavior behind an explicit opt-in until live probes confirm the account-specific ceiling and required headers.

blockers.concern: The PRD's central capability claim — that a 600K-token request to claude-fable-5-1 will succeed on this account — is never exercised. Every acceptance test for G-1 is a local pre-flight fixture with a mocked provider; the live probe is explicitly out of scope; the Appendix records as an unverified assumption that 1M context is available to this transport without a beta header. Anthropic long-context access has historically been tier-gated, beta-headed, and bounded by input-tokens-per-minute limits well below 600K/min.
blockers.why_matters: All Sprint 1 tests can be green while every real large /ride, red-team or BB call fails late with a 400/429 after the gate said 'warn'. G-1 would be declared met on evidence that measures the gate, not the model. Worse, a 429 on a 600K request that cheval retries re-sends 600K per attempt.
blockers.location: FR-1.1, FR-1.4, Goals G-1, Success Criteria G-1, Appendix 'Assumptions recorded'
blockers.recommendation: Add one cheap live evidence step that does not need the operator's key: a single ~250K-token streaming call through the subscription/headless hop, or have the SDD define a 'first large call' smoke in the E2E sprint whose failure is a stop condition. Record the account tier and ITPM limits in the catalog entry. Make retry-on-429 for requests above the probed ceiling a bounded single retry with the warning escalated to the envelope's error class rather than a full backoff loop.

blockers.concern: The document does not specify how catalog-derived limits are validated against provider-specific hard caps, SDK caps, CLI caps, gateway caps, or per-transport differences beyond streaming versus non-streaming.
blockers.why_matters: A catalog value may be correct abstractly but invalid for a specific adapter, SDK version, subscription path, or proxy, causing mismatched behavior between cheval, Bridgebuilder, Flatline, and provider APIs.
blockers.recommendation: Add a compatibility matrix and tests per provider and transport that verify input ceiling, output cap, timeout, beta headers, and token-count behavior against the actual invocation path.

blockers.concern: Using bytes-based token bounds when no Anthropic key is present is under-specified and may either undercount dangerous requests or overcount valid ones.
blockers.why_matters: Token estimation directly controls whether requests are sent, warned, or rejected; an inaccurate bound can cause provider failures, hidden truncation, or denial of valid large-context workflows.
blockers.recommendation: Specify the exact byte-to-token bound, prove it is conservative for each supported content type, add adversarial fixtures for Unicode and tool payloads, and record estimator uncertainty in envelopes.

blockers.concern: Warn-and-proceed for uncalibrated ceilings above the last probed value creates a broad failure mode for very large requests without a clear retry, chunking, or fallback strategy.
blockers.why_matters: Large runs may consume time and cost before failing, and unattended workflows may not recover if the provider rejects the request after cheval has already allowed it.
blockers.location: FR-1.1 Ceiling policy; Reliability; Risks & Mitigation
blockers.recommendation: Define deterministic recovery behavior for provider limit failures, including error classification, automatic downgrade to calibrated ceiling, optional chunking, and recording a calibration-needed event that prevents repeated blind retries.
